intro.text: The radio wakes on a frequency nobody uses: an old Navy band, all hiss and a patient Morse key. The same group repeats every forty seconds. The bridge decodes it as a bearing and a single word: [[byrd_1947:BEYOND]]. The signal is coming from below you, and it is getting stronger.
intro.radio: Auger, you are not cleared for that band. We will be on channel two.

options.text: Triangulate the source with the scanner.

answer.text: You tap back one group: RECEIVED. The keying stops. For a full minute there is nothing. Then the signal returns, slower, almost gentle, and spells out a route: depths, bearings, a warning about water. Your scanner fills in the next few kilometers. Something else, somewhere, was listening too.

mast.text: The helm runs three passes while the signal repeats. The source is not a transmitter. It is a mast of riveted aluminum thirty meters into solid granite, with a Navy plate older than anyone aboard. It has keyed the same word since before the rock closed over it.

silence.text: The bridge kills the receiver. The hiss is gone. In the quiet that follows, the hull ticks as it cools, and every tick sounds a little like Morse.
